posts.alt: Photo of the J. Edgar Hoover FBI Building in Washington, D.C., a large concrete office building under a blue sky. Text below reads: The FBI got hacked. Hackers reportedly broke into its crime database.
posts.caption:
Hackers reportedly got into the FBI's National Crime Information Center. That's the database police all over America lean on every single day.

NCIC is what an officer checks on a traffic stop. Warrants. Fugitives. Registered sex offenders. Whether someone failed a gun background check. Federal, state and local police all use it.

CNN broke the story. AP and Fox News reported it too, citing their own sources. The FBI is investigating. What the FBI hasn't done is say a word in public. Nobody knows yet what was taken, or who did it.

This is the second time in a few months. In September, a hacking group called ShinyHunters broke into the FBI's job portal.

And it lands in a rough stretch. A government watchdog just found 17 of 22 federal agencies out of compliance with federal cybersecurity rules.

Think about that. The agency that hunts hackers keeps getting hacked. If the FBI can't lock its own doors, who can?
posts.first:
President Trump said he had "just heard" about it when Kayleigh McEnany asked him on Fox News.

"I will say that it's not good. I don't like that," he said.

Then he found a silver lining only Trump would find. He said maybe the hack would turn up things nobody would have learned otherwise, and brought up the "Russia, Russia, Russia hoax."

The bigger worry is the cops. A retired FBI agent told Fox News a breach like this could put officers in danger during traffic stops, because they depend on NCIC to know who they're dealing with.

The FBI did not comment. Until it does, all of this comes from sources talking to reporters.

posts.alt: Official portrait photos side by side: President Donald Trump on the left and Texas Sen. John Cornyn on the right, split by a vertical white line. Text below reads: Sore loser. Cornyn lost his primary. Now he's blocking Trump's judge.
posts.caption:
John Cornyn lost his primary. Now a Trump judge is paying for it.

Sorry, but that's exactly how it looks from here.

President Trump nominated Elliot Gaiser for an open federal judgeship in Dallas. Gaiser runs the Justice Department's Office of Legal Counsel and clerked for Justice Samuel Alito. Cornyn is refusing to return his "blue slip," an old Senate custom that lets one home-state senator stop a district court pick cold.

And the clock matters. Republicans lose the Senate majority in January. Ted Cruz says Republicans agreed to confirm every judge they could before then, because he expects Democrats to block them all once they take over. Cruz says Cornyn "basically gave the seat to the Democrats."

Trump didn't hold back on Fox News: "He's a nice guy, John Cornyn, but he's doing a tremendous disservice because Gaiser is fantastic."

And: "We're going to have a radical left lunatic get in there, and we don't want that."
posts.first:
Cornyn's side: he says Trump waited until after the midterms, never consulted him, and picked "a non-Texan with little connection to the Lone Star State, with no trial court experience." He says he sent the White House another name.

Cruz says he asked Cornyn on the Senate floor to at least meet Gaiser, and Cornyn "got very angry. He began screaming. He began cursing at me."

Cornyn's answer on X: "Everyone knows that I am a notorious cusser and screamer and that Ted is a fragile thing. But enough about us."

Cornyn lost the primary to Ken Paxton, Trump's pick. Paxton then lost the seat to Democrat James Talarico. So a lame-duck Republican is holding up a Trump judge on his way out the door.

posts.quote: NEWSOM WANTS TO SAVE CALIFORNIA'S KILLERS.
posts.alt: Official portrait photo of California Gov. Gavin Newsom in a dark suit, standing in front of U.S. and California flags. Text below reads: Newsom wants to save California's killers. 30 DAs are suing to keep death row.
posts.caption:
Gavin Newsom is on his way out the door, and he wants to take California's entire death row with him. All 548 of them.

On November 5, Newsom announced he intends to commute every death sentence in the state to life without parole. According to the Death Penalty Information Center, it would be the largest mass commutation in American history. These are people juries sentenced to death for the worst murders in the state.

Now district attorneys from 30 counties are suing to stop it. The lawsuit, filed with the California Supreme Court by the Criminal Justice Legal Foundation along with victims' families, says Newsom never gave prosecutors and families the legal notice they were owed, or a chance to be heard.

Here's the part Newsom keeps skipping. California voters were asked to end the death penalty in 2012. They said no. They were asked again in 2016. They said no again.

Juries decided these cases one at a time. Newsom wants to wipe them all out at once, on his way out.
posts.first:
Who's on that list? Orange County DA Todd Spitzer filed his own challenge over 18 killers from his county. They include serial killer Randy Kraft and Alejandro Avila, who kidnapped and murdered 5-year-old Samantha Runnion in 2002.

"I refuse to allow one man to dismantle our criminal justice system brick by brick and sentence by sentence until there is not a shred of accountability left," Spitzer said.

Newsom calls it conscience. He wrote that clemency exists for moments when the law can't be squared with justice. "For me, this is that moment," he wrote.

For 382 of the inmates, the state Supreme Court has to sign off first. Attorney General Rob Bonta told the court nothing becomes final until the justices act.

posts.alt: Official portrait photo of Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez smiling in a black top, with a circle inset photo of the Hotel Bayerischer Hof in Munich. Text below reads: $12,000. One trip. AOC's 'fight the rich' tour went five-star.
posts.caption:
The congresswoman who wants to tax the rich sure knows how to travel like them.

Sorry, but somebody has to say it.

Federal Election Commission filings show Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez's campaign paid about $12,000 for her February trip to Germany. We pulled the filings ourselves. Here's the bill:

Hotel Bayerischer Hof in Munich: $5,250.73.
Westin Grand Berlin: $3,369.96.
A Berlin car company: $2,650.08.
Deutsche Bahn train tickets: $747.69.

The trip was for the Munich Security Conference, followed by a speech to students in Berlin. The Bayerischer Hof is one of Munich's landmark luxury hotels. Its guest list over the years includes Alfred Hitchcock and Grace Kelly.

Five-star Munich. A Westin in Berlin. A private car. Her campaign picked up the tab. That's campaign money. Donors gave it to her to win elections in the Bronx and Queens.

The New York Post first reported the spending and says her office didn't respond to questions.
posts.first:
To be fair about it: members of Congress are allowed to use campaign money for travel tied to their job, and her campaign listed these as "TRAVEL - OFFICIALLY CONNECTED." Nobody is saying she broke the law.

But this is a woman who calls herself a democratic socialist and has spent years telling the rest of us the rich don't pay their fair share. On this trip she demanded "material gains for the working class," according to the Post.

Material gains. Like a $5,250 hotel bill.

There's plenty of talk that she's building a foreign policy résumé for a 2028 run. She has denied it.

posts.alt: Photo of Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear in a dark suit speaking outdoors, with a crowd behind him. Text below reads: $1.5 billion. 'Flushed down the toilet.' Kentucky's auditor on Beshear's spending.
posts.caption:
Kentucky's state auditor says she found $1.5 billion in waste. She says Gov. Andy Beshear's answer was basically a shrug.

Auditor Allison Ball's office flagged $836 million in Medicaid waste, mostly from Kentucky paying monthly fees for people who were also enrolled in Medicaid in up to eight other states. Her audits also found one Social Security number being used by as many as 10 people, ineligible noncitizens getting benefits, and about $100 million in SNAP errors. An earlier audit found more than 330 dead people still on the Medicaid rolls.

And what did the governor's people say? Ball says she was told, "Well, that happens everywhere. You know, that's not unique to us."

"And that's really a troubling response," she said.

It happens everywhere. That's the excuse. Imagine telling your boss that about $836 million. Now imagine that guy wants to run the whole country, because Beshear is widely expected to run for president.
posts.first:
Beshear's office says Ball is wrong. It calls the $836 million figure "a wild extrapolation from a small subset" and says her report has "significant errors and inaccuracies." Back in March, his spokesperson said the auditor was "continuing to play political games."

Ball also flagged spending in Beshear's own executive branch for fiscal 2025: $183,576 in out-of-state travel, including a $7,632 limousine in Germany, and a $17,013 dinner at a Kentucky distillery. She said it wasn't illegal. She said it "needs to stop."

His office points to six straight budget surpluses and cuts to income and property taxes.

Ball told Fox News Digital she needs the public's help, because once the money is gone it usually can't be clawed back.
